regime_context: Detector shows a defensive/healthcare-led trend regime: Big Pharma is the co-leader with strong durability (0.84) and full breadth (1.0), surrounded by crowded equal-weight healthcare, consumer staples, and defensives. Leadership rank by itself has no forecast edge (rank-IC ~0 in backtest), and the macro narrative is dominated by AI-tech headlines that are disconnected from the defensive price trend — so this is a discipline/risk-control read, not a return call.
emerging_watch: Watch whether Memory/HBM (rank 1, score 1.712) actually transitions to eligible — currently eligible==false with durability_bar only 0.35 and breadth 0.0, so despite the top score it is NOT in the trend gate. The condition that retires this watch: Memory/HBM flips eligible==true with breadth rising above 0.5 before Big Pharma's rotation margin narrows further.

theses.subject: Big Pharma
theses.thesis: Big Pharma is the only leader with both an eligible absolute-trend gate and maximum breadth (1.0), with the highest durability bar (0.84) among eligible themes, and it is the current rotation challenger closing on Memory/HBM. That makes it the cleanest expression of the defensive-trend structure without betting on the ineligible Memory leader. Crowding (z=1.46) is a sizing caution only, not a fade signal.
theses.dissent: PPH is already crowded (z=1.46) and the theme has led the defensive rotation for long enough that momentum-extension risk is elevated; any macro risk-on rotation out of healthcare would hurt the crowded leader hardest.

falsifier.text: PPH breaks below its own 50-day average and breadth drops below 0.7 before the 20-day check-by date

theses.subject: Defensives
theses.thesis: Defensives is eligible with high durability (0.82) and near-full breadth (0.944), and it clusters with the healthcare/staples leadership structure. It names the broad defensive trend that is confirmed across multiple equal-weight sector themes, not just one crowded ETF.
theses.dissent: This is an unscorable basket (proxy is a list, no single ETF), so the observable is fuzzy; and crowdedness across defensives suggests the easy defensive move may already be made.

falsifier.text: XLP and XLU both lag SPY by 3% or more before the 20-day check-by date

check.reason: theme has no scalar etf_proxy → not cleanly scorable

theses.subject: US Energy Complex
theses.thesis: US Energy Complex is one of the few eligible themes with a trend tag AND low crowding (z=0.31, crowded==false), standing apart from the crowded defensive complex. Its durability bar (0.48) is weaker than healthcare, but it is the only eligible non-crowded trend expression available, offering a cleaner risk-control entry than the crowded leaders.
theses.dissent: Breadth is 0.0, meaning the trend is not broad-based across the complex — it may be driven by one or two names, and the macro narrative shows only one energy headline in the recent window.

falsifier.text: XLE breadth remains at zero and XLE lags SPY by 4% before the 15-day check-by date

macro_narrative.note: market-level macro/policy/geo narrative flow; coincident, not per-theme, never a trigger
